# opencode-hard-limit Stop [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) before it burns through your AI quota. `opencode-hard-limit` is a plugin that watches your Claude/Anthropic and OpenAI usage and puts a **hard stop** on model calls once you drop below a percent-remaining threshold you choose. It also adds a live **sidebar bar** so you can see exactly how much you have left and when the window resets. It reads your subscription quota **natively** without an external quota plugin, then adds the enforcement layer: a hard stop plus a live sidebar bar. **Works on OpenCode 2.x and 1.x.** Since 0.19.0 one package serves both major versions, and `install` detects which one you run. See [OpenCode 2.x](#opencode-2x). ## Why you might want this Quota runs out at the worst possible time. Two common situations this is built for: - **Shared quota, no surprises.** When a team splits one plan, you rarely want any single person to sprint to 100%. Set the goal so everyone stops with a buffer left (for example, block once 70% is used so 30% stays for the rest of the team). - **Runaway prompts.** A single bloated prompt or an over-eager agent loop can drain a window shockingly fast. A hard stop keeps one bad turn from wiping out your whole budget. **Your goal is a single number: the minimum percent you want to keep in reserve.** That is the `threshold`. Everything else has a sensible default. ## Quick start One command. It writes your config, registers the plugin for auto-update, and wires up the sidebar: ```sh npx opencode-hard-limit init --global --threshold 30 --install ``` Then **restart OpenCode**. That is it. This is all you need if you use one Claude account and one OpenAI account. If you switch between several logins, see [Multi-account](#multi-account). `install` does three things: 1. **Registers the server plugin:** writes `"opencode-hard-limit"` into `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`. OpenCode reads this on every startup and automatically fetches the latest published version via its native package manager, so the hard-stop logic is always up to date without any manual steps. 2. **Deploys the sidebar widget:** copies `quota-sidebar.tsx` into `~/.config/opencode/plugins/` and registers it in `tui.json`. The plugin factory also self-heals the sidebar on every opencode startup: it checks whether the deployed file matches the currently installed npm version and re-copies it if not, so sidebar and server plugin stay in sync automatically. 3. **Registers the CLI:** when the server plugin starts, it installs the matching published package globally in the background. This makes `opencode-hard-limit` available in OpenCode shell mode for commands such as `opencode-hard-limit postpone 30`. There is **no external quota dependency**. The plugin reads quota itself: for Claude/Anthropic it uses the selected local account's OAuth credentials when available and can use the local `claude` CLI for legacy single-account access. For OpenAI it uses the OAuth session in OpenCode's `auth.json` or a supported multi-account store. Nothing to install separately. Prefer to be walked through it? Run `npx opencode-hard-limit init` with no flags. It asks **where** the threshold should apply (global or project) and prints the next step. `init` without `--install` only writes config; run `npx opencode-hard-limit install` afterward to activate the plugin. `init` and `install` also ask, **once**, whether to star the repo on GitHub: ```text ★ Star the repo on GitHub? (Y/n) ``` It only ever asks on an interactive terminal, and only starts a star after an explicit yes by calling your own already-authenticated [`gh`](https://cli.github.com/) (`gh api --method PUT /user/starred/...`). The plugin never handles a GitHub token of its own. Answering either way is remembered in `~/.config/opencode/opencode-hard-limit/star-prompted`, so you are not asked again. To never see it: pass `--no-star`, or set `OPENCODE_QUOTA_NO_STAR=1` (`CI` is honored too). Without `gh` installed or authenticated it just prints the URL. ## OpenCode 2.x Since 0.19.0 the plugin runs natively on OpenCode 2.x (tested on 2.2.5), and the same package still serves 1.x (1.18.29 or newer). OpenCode 2 does not run 1.x plugins and reads a different config key. The easiest path is `npx opencode-hard-limit install`, which picks the right key. To do it by hand on 2.x, add the package to `plugins` (not `plugin`) in `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json(c)`: ```jsonc { "plugins": ["opencode-hard-limit"] } ``` That single entry loads both parts: the hard stop (a gate on the `context`, `compaction` and `generate` model requests) and the sidebar (exported as `opencode-hard-limit/tui`). Do not also list the sidebar in `cli.json`, and remove any old `quota-sidebar.tsx` entry there, or it shows twice. For a local checkout, use the absolute path of the repo directory instead of the package name. Config changes apply without a restart. `opencode-hard-limit install` does this for you: it detects the OpenCode version, writes `plugins` on 2.x and `plugin` on 1.x, and on 2.x also removes the old 1.x sidebar copy and its `tui.json`/`cli.json` entries. It writes `opencode.json`; if you keep your config in `opencode.jsonc`, add the entry there by hand instead. ## What's new in 0.18.0 With a single account, nothing changes for you: no new setup, same `threshold`. The release adds: - **Multi-account quota.** Named Claude profiles and OpenAI account stores are read per account, the gate checks the account that serves each request, and the sidebar shows one row per account. See [Multi-account](#multi-account). - **Gentler 429 handling.** A server-sent `Retry-After` is capped (`maxRateLimitBackoffMs`, 10 min; `noBaselineRateLimitBackoffMs`, 1 min when there is no earlier reading). - **A transient error no longer blocks on its own.** On a timeout, 5xx, or malformed response the gate keeps using the last good reading. It blocks only when that reading is below the threshold, or when it is too old and close to the threshold (the stale fail-safe, see `staleBlockMarginPct`). - **Expired profile tokens pass through.** A named Claude profile whose OAuth token has expired is allowed through with a warning, so the call itself can renew the token. - **`warm` and `warm --watch`.** Opt-in commands that keep idle Claude profiles logged in. They never run unless you call them. See [`warm`](#refreshing-idle-claude-profiles-warm). ## Updating Updates arrive automatically. Once you have run `install`, OpenCode checks for a newer published version of `opencode-hard-limit` on every startup and updates the server plugin in the background. The sidebar self-heals to match on the same or next restart, with no manual steps needed. If you are upgrading from a version prior to `0.9.0` (which used file copies instead of the native plugin registry), run the installer once to migrate: ```sh npx opencode-hard-limit@latest install ``` That removes the old copied files, registers the package for auto-update, and redeploys the sidebar. After that you are on the automatic update path. ## Uninstall One line removes every file and unregisters the sidebar and server plugin: ```sh npx opencode-hard-limit uninstall ``` Restart OpenCode to finish. Your saved threshold and the shared TUI runtime dependencies are left in place (other plugins may use them). ## How it works Before every model request, on OpenCode's `chat.params` hook: 1. Detect the provider. IDs containing `anthropic` or `claude` map to Anthropic; IDs containing `openai` or `codex` map to OpenAI. Anything else passes through. 2. Resolve one account with the shared account resolver. Each quota result has its own `provider:accountKey:window` cache slot. 3. Use fresh cached quota on the hot path. If there is no cached result yet, perform one protected fetch so the first request is still guarded. 4. Refresh quota mostly when a session goes idle (`session.status=idle` / `session.idle`), with spacing controlled by `minRefreshIntervalMs`. 5. On a 429, honor a server `Retry-After` up to `maxRateLimitBackoffMs`. Without a `Retry-After`, use the configured `rateLimitBackoffMs` as-is. If there is no last-known-good reading, the server delay is instead capped by the smaller of `maxRateLimitBackoffMs` and `noBaselineRateLimitBackoffMs`. With a last-known-good value, return that value marked stale during the backoff. Without one, a rate-limit error fails open. 6. A transient non-auth failure, such as a timeout, 5xx, or malformed response, also serves the last-known-good reading as stale. An auth error is not hidden behind a value that cannot be refreshed. When a stale reading is served, the transient error does not invoke `blockOnError`; the ordinary threshold still blocks if that reading is already below the threshold. 7. Block when known quota is below `threshold`. A stale successful reading can trigger the separate stale-failsafe when quota is blind and the remaining percentage is within `staleBlockMarginPct` of the threshold. `blockOnError` governs timeout and unknown errors when there is no successful value to serve. `blockOnAuthError` governs auth and unreadable errors. `cacheTtlMs` controls how long a quota result is considered fresh for the refresh path. The stale-failsafe is distinct from `blockOnError` and can block when a stale quota value is close to the threshold. ## Which window: 5h or weekly By **default the plugin watches the rolling 5h window**, so a burst of heavy usage trips the limit quickly and recovers a few hours later. Prefer to pace yourself across the whole week instead? Switch to the weekly window: ```sh # Track the weekly window globally npx opencode-hard-limit set --window Weekly --global # Back to the default 5h window npx opencode-hard-limit set --window 5h --global ``` Both the hard-stop and the sidebar follow whichever window you set. ### Per-provider window override Not every account exposes both windows. Some ChatGPT/Codex accounts only expose a **Weekly** window (no rolling 5h window at all), while Anthropic typically exposes both. Rather than force one global `--window` for every provider, you can override the window for just one provider and let the other keep inheriting the base `--window`: ```sh # OpenAI/Codex account only has a Weekly window; keep Claude on the default 5h npx opencode-hard-limit set --window-openai Weekly --global # Or pin Claude to Weekly while OpenAI stays on 5h npx opencode-hard-limit set --window-anthropic Weekly --global ``` `--window-anthropic` / `--window-openai` (env: `OPENCODE_QUOTA_WINDOW_ANTHROPIC` / `OPENCODE_QUOTA_WINDOW_OPENAI`) take precedence over the base `--window` for that provider only, at every config layer (env > project > global > default). If unset, the provider simply inherits `--window`. `opencode-hard-limit get` shows `(inherits window)` for any per-provider key that isn't explicitly set. ### Automatic fallback when the requested window doesn't exist If the requested window (whether from `--window` or an explicit per-provider override) simply doesn't exist on your account, the plugin automatically falls back to whichever window the account *does* expose instead of erroring out, silently. The sidebar shows the effective window that's actually being used (e.g. `OpenAI Weekly 92% left, limit 25%`), which is the only signal you'll get; there is no toast. To pin the provider to the window your account actually exposes: ```sh opencode-hard-limit set --window-openai Weekly --global ``` Once set explicitly to a window your account has, the request succeeds directly with no fallback needed. ## Sidebar usage bar The install step also registers a small SolidJS TUI widget in OpenCode's sidebar. For each monitored provider it shows: - A usage bar with the percent remaining for your configured window. - Your threshold, so you can see how close you are. - A color that shifts from green to red as you approach the limit. - A `Resets in Xh Ymin` line so you know when the window rolls over. It reads the **same** threshold and window as the hard-stop (no extra config), polls every 120s by default (`OPENCODE_QUOTA_SIDEBAR_POLL_MS` override), and appears after you restart OpenCode. With several accounts the sidebar shows one row per account, labeled with the account name (see [Multi-account](#multi-account)). Rows for accounts that disappear are removed on the next refresh.
Why the widget ships as raw .tsx (not bundled) OpenCode transpiles the raw `.tsx` with babel-preset-solid and virtualizes `@opentui/solid`, `@opentui/core`, and `solid-js` at the package level. That is the only supported path. Pre-bundling emits `from "@opentui/solid/jsx-runtime"`, a subpath OpenCode does not virtualize, which would put JSX on a separate solid-js instance from the virtualized `createSignal` and make the widget render nothing silently. So the installer copies the source and ensures the three TUI runtime deps exist in `~/.config/opencode/`.
## Multi-account **Only read this if you use more than one Claude or OpenAI account.** With a single account, the [Quick start](#quick-start) is all you need and nothing on this page applies to you. The plugin can read multiple Claude and OpenAI accounts from their local account stores. It never creates or logs in accounts itself, and it does not depend on any account-management plugin. It only reads what those tools leave on disk: - **Claude, one login per profile.** A plugin such as [`@openchamber/opencode-claude`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@openchamber/opencode-claude) runs several isolated Claude Code logins, one instance per profile, each with its own `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` (for example `~/.claude-profiles/pro` and `~/.claude-profiles/max`). Each instance registers a provider ID such as `claude-pro` or `claude-max`. - **Claude, rotating accounts.** A manager plugin that keeps a single `anthropic` provider and switches the active account can write a store at `~/.config/opencode/anthropic-multi-account-accounts.json`. If that file exists, the plugin follows whichever account is marked active (`activeAccountUuid`). Set `anthropicAccountsFile` to use another path. - **OpenAI.** [`oc-codex-multi-auth`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/oc-codex-multi-auth) keeps its accounts in `~/.opencode/oc-codex-multi-auth-accounts.json`. ### Set up named Claude profiles 1. Create one profile per login with your account plugin, so that each profile ends up with its own `.credentials.json`, for example `~/.claude-profiles/pro/.credentials.json`. The directory name after `~/.claude-profiles/` is the profile slug. 2. Make sure the provider ID of each profile ends with its slug: `claude-pro` is checked against profile `pro`, `claude-max` against `max`. 3. Run `opencode-hard-limit accounts` and confirm every profile is listed with its remaining quota. 4. Restart OpenCode. The sidebar now shows one row per account. Nothing else is required: profile mode switches on by itself as soon as one named profile is found, or when you set `anthropicProfileDirs`. ### What is read where - **Claude profiles:** each named profile lives at `~/.claude-profiles//.credentials.json`. Configure other locations with `anthropicProfileDirs`, using the `--anthropic-profile-dirs` CLI option, the `OPENCODE_QUOTA_ANTHROPIC_PROFILE_DIRS` environment variable, or an array in the config file. Provider IDs such as `claude-pro` and `claude-max` map to profiles `pro` and `max`. Profile directories with the same OAuth refresh token are deduplicated, so a copied profile does not create a second account. - **OpenAI accounts:** the plugin reads the account store at `~/.opencode/oc-codex-multi-auth-accounts.json` by default. Set `openaiAccountsFile` with `--openai-accounts-file`, the `OPENCODE_QUOTA_OPENAI_ACCOUNTS_FILE` environment variable, or the config file to use another path. List discovered accounts with `opencode-hard-limit accounts`, or use `opencode-hard-limit accounts --json` for structured output. There is also an opt-in mode called **fail-postpone**, a manual, time-boxed bypass of a quota block for when you accept the risk of running over quota for a little while. It's disabled by default. Enable it with: ```bash opencode-hard-limit set --allow-postpone true --global ``` Once enabled, a block's error message includes a hint like: ``` [quota-hard-stop] Blocked claude-max (anthropic:cp:max (Claude Max)): quota 12% remaining is below the 30% threshold. ... To postpone this block: in OpenCode, type ! by itself first to enter shell mode. Pasting a whole "!opencode-hard-limit ..." line at once will not trigger it, so type the ! yourself, then paste the rest. Run: opencode-hard-limit postpone (default 30, e.g. "opencode-hard-limit postpone 60"). This has no LLM cost. ``` The part in parentheses names the account that was read. With a single account it is short, for example `Blocked anthropic (anthropic)`. **Important: type the `!`, don't paste it.** OpenCode only enters shell mode when `!` is the first character *typed* into an empty prompt. If you copy the whole `!opencode-hard-limit postpone 60` line (with the `!`) and paste it in one go, OpenCode will **not** switch to shell mode. The paste lands as a normal chat message instead. To run the command correctly: 1. Type `!` yourself (one keystroke, empty prompt) to enter shell mode. 2. Paste (or type) just `opencode-hard-limit postpone 60`, without the leading `!`. 3. Press Enter. This postpones **any** quota block (any provider, any window) for 60 minutes. Cancel it early the same way: type `!`, then paste: ``` opencode-hard-limit postpone --clear ``` `opencode-hard-limit get` shows whether a postpone is currently active and how much time is left. Postpone duration is clamped to 1–240 minutes. If `--allow-postpone` is later disabled, any leftover postpone timer is ignored. Blocks resume immediately. The sidebar widget also shows a red two-line hint ("To postpone the blockage for 30 min: type ! then paste: opencode-hard-limit postpone 30") whenever a monitored provider is currently blocked and fail-postpone is enabled but not active. It disappears automatically once you postpone or once quota refreshes above the threshold. **Known limitation: subagents.** If a subagent (e.g. one dispatched via OpenCode's `task` tool) is the one whose call gets blocked, its parent orchestrator currently sees an **empty** result instead of this message. OpenCode's `task` tool only returns the subagent's generated text; since this plugin blocks *before* any text is generated, there's nothing for the task tool to relay. This is a gap in OpenCode itself (tracked upstream), not something this plugin can work around. If a subagent's task mysteriously returns empty, check `opencode-hard-limit get` or the sidebar for an active block. ## Requirements - OpenCode with plugin support. - **Claude/Anthropic quota:** a Claude Pro/Max OAuth login available through a supported local account source. Pure API-key/PAYG usage has no subscription window and reads as `unavailable` by design. `warm` additionally requires the local `claude` CLI. - **OpenAI quota:** a ChatGPT session token in OpenCode's `auth.json` or a supported multi-account store. An API-plan OAuth token reads as `unavailable` by design. - Network access when a live quota check runs (the usage endpoints). - **Multi-account (optional):** see [Multi-account](#multi-account) above. Nothing extra to install; the plugin detects supported local account stores. ## Verify it works Force a block by setting the threshold above your current remaining: ```sh OPENCODE_QUOTA_MIN_REMAINING=90 opencode ``` With, say, 81% remaining, the next Claude/OpenAI call is blocked. Set it back to `30` (or unset) for normal operation. ## Upgrade Once installed via `npx opencode-hard-limit install`, updates arrive automatically on every OpenCode startup, with no manual steps needed. See the [Updating](#updating) section above for details and migration from older versions. ## License MIT
